slices.brief: WS01 slice 29 of 32 (checkpoint D, the design system; slices 20 to 32; its draft PR is #108). Branch redesign/ws01-design-system, HEAD c534742 (slice 28); the base for diffs is c534742. Checkpoints A, B and C are merged to main and live. test/unit/redesign-status-step28.test.ts (all of it: the date line at 108 to 115, the follow-up counts at 330 to 340, the decisions count at 243 and the spec sentence at 356 to 377) with the earlier record tests, so the flag-off baseline comparison stays green. The lead's notes win over this brief and the manifest where they differ (they say nothing on this slice beyond the standing rules and one note for step 32 on the baseline sampler, which every step must leave alone: difference 13): <scratchpad>/ws01-lead-notes.md. The manifest entry (order 29) is in <scratchpad>/ws01-manifest.json. node_modules is installed; nothing ever runs against a remote database or the Cloudflare account; agents never commit, stash, reset or check out anything; the working tree is the only copy. Environment facts for this container: the pinned Playwright expects a Chromium build the container does not have, so every npm run test:a11y here runs as PW_CHROMIUM_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers/chromium npm run test:a11y (the config reads that variable); never run playwright install; WRANGLER_SEND_METRICS=false on every wrangler command; localhost is exempt from the outbound proxy, so the a11y servers on 127.0.0.1 work. Dependencies are exact-pinned (no caret) at versions at least two weeks old (today is 2026-10-21, so published on or before 2026-10-07), with package-lock.json updated by npm install; this slice adds two development dependencies, sharp and lighthouse (differences 3 and 4). The branch tip is c534742 (slice 28), and the working tree is clean when the slice starts; origin/redesign/ws01-design-system carries later commits only once the lead pushes, and the local main ref does not carry the checkpoint merges, so a diff against the local main shows far more than this slice: take this slice's own changes as the working tree against c534742. A full test:a11y run and the lab check each start servers on ports 8801 and 8802 over the one database in .wrangler/a11y, so never run two of them at once. Build exactly this. End auto-advance and build the image pipeline. scripts/images.mjs, with sharp as an exact-pinned devDependency run by hand, writes AVIF and WebP at 640, 1024 and 1600 widths for src/assets/LCA_Slide_1.jpg to LCA_Slide_5.jpg into src/assets/generated/. Quality is tuned so the file a 390 px phone at DPR 3 picks is at most 200 KB. The outputs are committed, so builds never need sharp. hero.png is skipped because nothing imports it. src/components/ResponsiveImage.tsx renders <picture> with AVIF and WebP sources, sizes, explicit width and height from the source dimensions, fetchpriority="high" for the LCP image and loading="lazy" otherwise. In HomePage.tsx, when newLook is on, HeroSlideshow is not rendered. The hero shows one static ResponsiveImage (slide 1) with the existing heading and actions, and no timer exists. With the flag off, today's slideshow remains. WS03 replaces the hero entirely. test/unit/no-rotation.test.ts fails on setInterval or setTimeout loops that rotate content in src TSX, with an allowlist for AdminEmailPage's history poll and AnnualMeetingPage's minute clock; HomePage's flag-off path is listed until WS03 deletes it. npm run perf:home runs Lighthouse (exact-pinned devDependency) in mobile mode against the a11y-on server and prints the performance score. K also runs a lab check on the preview, and both are recorded in REDESIGN_STATUS.md. Verify items from the manifest, each to be re-checked against the tree as it is now (the earlier finding follows): Hero weight and auto-advance. (Five slides total 2,171 KB (569, 303, 519, 290 and 490 KB; 2048 px wide). HeroSlideshow in HomePage.tsx calls setInterval(..., 5000) at lines 53 and 56, with no pause control and no reduced-motion check. hero.png (343 x 361, 13 KB) is not imported anywhere. Re-checked: the sizes hold: LCA_Slide_1.jpg to LCA_Slide_5.jpg are 569,165, 303,072, 518,776, 290,367 and 489,640 bytes (2,171,020 in all), each 2048 pixels wide, but they are not one shape: 2048 by 1237 (slide 1), 2048 by 1536 (slides 2, 3 and 5) and 2048 by 882 (slide 4); the two setInterval calls are at HomePage.tsx lines 53 (in restart, run by the arrows and dots) and 56 (in the effect, whose empty dependency list is lint warning 58); nothing in HomePage.tsx or any file it draws pauses it or reads a reduced-motion setting, and src/index.css's reduced-motion rule (lines 759 to 773) sets only CSS durations to zero and only under :root[data-look="new"], so it would not stop an interval even with the switch on; hero.png is 343 by 361 and 13,057 bytes and no file under src, test, scripts or index.html names it. The five photos are not img elements: each is a CSS background-image (HomePage.tsx line 73, an inline style) on a div in a flex track that slides sideways by translateX, so all five download at once on every visit, 2,171 KB, whichever slide shows; see difference 1.) Other timers. (setInterval also appears in AdminEmailPage.tsx:196 (history poll) and AnnualMeetingPage.tsx:80 (minute clock); neither rotates content. Re-checked: both hold, at AdminEmailPage.tsx line 196 (setInterval(loadHistory, 3000), only while a campaign is sending) and AnnualMeetingPage.tsx line 80 (a 60-second clock for the countdown); the finding leaves out a third, src/hooks/useNow.ts line 17, a 30-second refresh of the price clock drawn by TournamentDetailPage.tsx line 266 and FamilyRegistrationPanel.tsx line 54, in a .ts file; see difference 7.) PageHero without any slideshow. (PageHero.tsx has no slideshow; its header comment says the HomePage slideshow is separate. Nothing to remove there. Re-checked: it holds; src/components/PageHero.tsx draws no image at all, its comment at line 19 reads 'NOT for the HomePage slideshow hero', and 12 files import it.) Further differences between the manifest's assumptions and the tree, all measured at the tree this slice starts from (slice 28 finished). (1) There is no image element to turn into a picture; the hero's photos are backgrounds, and nothing in src uses srcset, sizes or picture. HomePage.tsx draws the photo as a div with backgroundImage: `url(${slide.src})` (line 73), darkened by an inline filter of grayscale(35%) brightness(0.55) contrast(1.05) (line 74) and a scale of 1.04 (line 75), under a navy veil of bg-brand-navy/55 mix-blend-multiply (line 79) and a bottom gradient (line 81), in a box that is 420 pixels high by an inline style (line 65), and the words and buttons are a sibling layer over it (lines 88 to 112). The whole of src holds 16 img elements in 13 files (LcaLogo, FacebookFeed, Footer, Navbar, PostsPanel twice, OfficerPhoto, WorkspacePage, AdminClubPage, AdminEmailPage, NewsPostPage, NewsPage, ScannerPage three times, ClubsPage), none of them a hero, and no picture, source or srcset anywhere. So the still hero is the first picture on the site. It has to carry the same darkening (the filter string and the scale as a style on the img, the veil and gradient layers over it) so the hero looks as it does today and the contrast test's reading of it (a photo no lighter than #40444c) stays true; the img fills the 420-pixel box with object-fit cover and a centred position, as bg-cover bg-center does today. The hero is the only place a photo is a hero: ClubDetailPage.tsx's hero holds a club's logo tile as a CSS background (line 163, a URL a club uploaded) and AdminClubPage.tsx's hero has no image. (2) The slides are not alike, and the 200 KB phone budget is a property of the 1600-pixel file. At 390 px wide and DPR 3 the device needs 1170 pixels, so with sizes of 100vw the browser takes the smallest file of 1170 or more, the 1600-pixel one; with the box fixed at 420 px high and a cover fit, slide 1 (a 1.656 shape) is drawn 695 CSS pixels wide on a 390-pixel phone, so its 1600-pixel file is already upscaled there and a sizes value of max(100vw, 696px) says so truthfully; either way the same file is picked at DPR 3, and the choice shows at DPR 2 (1024 or 1600). The sharp encoder was run here on slide 1 and the others in memory only (nothing written), so the size of what the script will write is known: slide 1 at 1600 pixels is 116,652 bytes as AVIF at quality 50 and 174,677 at quality 60, 175,804 as WebP at quality 75; at 1024 pixels 66,516 (AVIF 50), 97,915 (AVIF 60) and 92,552 (WebP 75); at 640 pixels 33,763 (AVIF 50), 48,580 (AVIF 60) and 44,420 (WebP 75); its heights come out 386, 619 and 966 pixels. At 1600 pixels and AVIF 60 or WebP 75 slides 3 and 5 are over 200 KB (AVIF 245,201 and 225,121; WebP 264,114 and 229,892), slide 2 is 155,825 and 161,168 and slide 4 is 98,055 and 103,612. The manifest asks only that the file a phone picks for the hero be 200 KB or less, which slide 1 meets at quality 60; this slice holds every one of the 30 files to 200,000 bytes (so either reading of '200 KB' passes) with a per-image or per-width quality table in the script, since WS03 or a later page may draw any slide; record the table. (3) sharp is already installed, and the manifest's proxy install is not needed. node_modules/sharp is 0.34.5, a development dependency of miniflare (wrangler's local runtime, which pins it exactly: package-lock.json line 10357; the entry at line 11878 is marked dev), with its linux-x64 binaries in node_modules/@img, and it writes AVIF (its heif format lists the .avif suffix; libheif 1.20.2 with aom 3.13.1) and WebP; package.json does not list it. npm says the latest is 0.35.5 (published 2026-09-27, 24 days ago, node ^18.17.0 || ^20.3.0 || >=21.0.0). 0.34.5 was published 2025-11-06, well over two weeks ago. Pin the one the lockfile already holds: npm install --save-dev --save-exact sharp@0.34.5, which adds the line to package.json and the root entry of the lockfile and adds no second copy and no download; installing 0.35.5 would put a second sharp and its native binaries beside miniflare's. Say in the record which version was chosen and why, and that 0.35.5 exists. sharp is run by hand (node scripts/images.mjs, with an npm script if you like); no file under src, test, functions or the build configuration imports it, the outputs are committed, and test/unit/image-budget.test.ts reads sizes from the files and widths from their headers rather than importing sharp, so a build or a test run never loads it. (4) The lab check's package is not installed anywhere and has to be fetched. lighthouse is at 13.5.0 (published 2026-09-18, 33 days ago; node >=22.19; about 19 MB unpacked); 13.4.1 is 2026-07-20; it depends on chrome-launcher (^1.2.1; the latest, 1.2.2, was published 2026-09-29, 22 days ago, and 1.2.1 on 2025-09-25). Pin lighthouse at 13.5.0, exact, through the proxy; the container runs node 22.22.0 and CI's node-version '22' takes the newest 22, so the engine range holds. The script must launch a browser: either pin chrome-launcher exactly (1.2.2) as a direct development dependency, or start the container's Chromium itself (PW_CHROMIUM_PATH, the variable playwright.config.ts reads, with a remote debugging port and the no-sandbox flag a root container needs) and hand lighthouse the port; say which and why. scripts/perf-home.ts runs with node --no-warnings --experimental-strip-types like scripts/check-bundle.ts (npm run perf:home); scripts/*.ts are in no tsconfig's include list, so nothing typechecks them, but eslint does lint them (the TypeScript block covers every .ts file), so they must lint clean. No script today starts the a11y-on server outside Playwright: perf-home.ts may import buildVariant, A11Y_VARIANTS, a11yServerArgs, A11Y_SERVER_ENV, A11Y_PERSIST and ROOT from test/a11y/global-setup.ts (importing runs nothing), build the a11y-on variant, and start wrangler pages dev on it itself, local only, then stop it; it must not run beside test:a11y (one database folder, two ports), and must say so in its header. It runs the mobile preset against /, prints the performance score and the LCP element and its time, and the score is a recorded lab measurement, not a gate (the manifest's risk: scores in a container vary widely; record the runs). (5) Importing an AVIF file will not typecheck yet. src/vite-env.d.ts declares png, jpg, jpeg, webp, svg and css modules and no avif, and tsconfig.app.json does not load the bundler's client types, so tsc -b (the first half of npm run build) fails on an import of a .avif file until src/vite-env.d.ts gains a declare module for *.avif. That file is outside the manifest's list; add the declaration and record the file. The bundler already treats avif and webp as assets (hashed names, emitted to dist/assets, inlined only under 4096 bytes, and none of the files is that small), and no image plugin is configured. How the component reaches the 30 files decides what ships: explicit imports of slide 1's six files emit 6 more files to dist/assets (127 now, 133 after) while an import.meta.glob over src/assets/generated emits all 30 (157) into every build, the flag-off build included; choose the explicit imports, which keep the other 24 out of dist, and report the file count and bytes before and after. (6) HomePage.tsx is pinned by seven tests, and they decide how the file may change. Whatever the still hero is, the pill, the heading, the words, the two buttons and the three figures (lines 88 to 112) and the data-ground="dark" marker (line 65) exist in the file once, drawn by the slideshow and by the still alike, with only the photo layers and the controls different: a second copy would make a second text-gold-on-dark-badge pill (contrast.test.ts expects exactly one, goldAllowlist.ts counts one), a second marked node (contrast.test.ts and semantic-map-grounds.test.ts expect exactly one in HomePage.tsx; tokens.spec.ts expects exactly one on /), and move the raw-colours allowlist's HomePage counts (bg-white/10 and hover:bg-white/20 on the Join LCA button, one each). The slideshow stays in HomePage.tsx for the flag-off path (moving HeroSlideshow to another file moves its seven allowlist entries, 9 uses, which name src/pages/HomePage.tsx), and its slide controls (bg-white/20 twice, bg-white/40, hover:bg-white/30 twice, hover:bg-white/60) stay written there once. The still branch keeps a bg-brand-navy/55 layer inside the marked element, the filter string 'grayscale(35%) brightness(0.55) contrast(1.05)' as written, and to-black/10. Adding lines above line 208 moves the trophy that goldText.test.ts pins at HomePage.tsx:208 (lines 1148 and 1154), so move that pin in the same change, or keep line 208 where it is. HomePage.tsx names no LcaMark, LcaLogo or lca-logo (brand-edges.test.tsx), keeps its own StatusDot function (base-components-scope.test.ts) and its one fetch (area-boundaries.test.ts), and imports the switch the way Footer.tsx does (import { FEATURES } from '@/lib/features'; it does not import it today). No test renders HomePage today and none names HeroSlideshow, Slide, slideshow, carousel, srcset or picture (a search of test and scripts finds only the known-violations selectors, the raw-colours allowlist reasons, one comment in semantic-map-grounds.test.ts, and LcaLogo's own no-picture test in brand-edges.test.tsx), so the flag-off test holds today's hero as literal strings copied from HomePage.tsx before you edit it, in a fixture beside the test (test/unit/fixtures/home-hero-today.ts), and flips the switch inside one file with the hoisted getter of news-pinned-flag.test.tsx; HomePage needs the auth context and the database client mocked and its fetch calls answered, as other page tests do. (7) The timer test has a rule to follow, and a third interval to place. The rule must be mechanical: scan every .ts and .tsx file under src (not tsx alone, because useNow.ts is a hook); every setInterval must be named in an allowlist with its reason and its count; a setTimeout that schedules itself again, or whose callback starts the function it sits in, is a loop and fails. Today: setInterval at HomePage.tsx lines 53 and 56 (the flag-off slideshow, listed until WS03 deletes it, count 2), AdminEmailPage.tsx:196, AnnualMeetingPage.tsx:80 and src/hooks/useNow.ts:17 (a price clock, not a rotation); setTimeout calls that are not loops: UscfSearchInput.tsx:177 (a debounce), FamilyRegistrationPanel.tsx:126 (a reload after 1200 ms), ResetPasswordPage.tsx:51 and 91 (a one-shot give-up), TournamentsPage.tsx:456 (a scroll), ScannerPage.tsx:589 and 614, clubMap.ts:84. Pin the allowlist by file and count, not by line, and prove the scan fails on planted cases in a temporary tree (a setInterval in a TSX, one in a .ts hook, a recursive setTimeout, a count one higher than allowed) with the names put together when the test runs, as raw-colours.test.ts does. (8) What AC4 can and cannot say. The reduced-motion rule is the new look's alone (:root[data-look="new"]), so with the switch off a visitor who asks for reduced motion still gets the slideshow, as today; with it on there is no slideshow, no timer and no transition on the hero, so AC4 is proved on a11y-on. The browser half reads document.getAnimations() on / and on the fixture page (/__fixtures/base, in the a11y builds only) after interactions (focus and hover on the hero's buttons, a scroll, a click that opens and closes nothing that navigates) with reducedMotion set to reduce, and expects none; if the loading line's spinner or a dialog leaves one, wait for what the test reads to be drawn first, and if one still remains record it as a finding. A page clock (page.clock.install before the page loads, then fastForward by 60 seconds) shows the hero's picture, its srcset and its box unchanged. (9) 'Every img rendered on / has width and height' holds only with newLook on. On a11y-on / draws two: the hero's and the footer's LcaLogo (width and height 56); the header's brand mark is an svg, and the home page's feed band uses FacebookFeed's compact variant, which draws no img (the one img it can draw, FacebookFeed.tsx line 212 in the full variant on /news, has no width or height; record it as a follow-up older than the step, not changed here, since it is not on /). With newLook off the header's img (Navbar.tsx line 240) and the footer's (Footer.tsx line 62) set their size with classes and carry no width or height attribute: that is today's markup, unchanged, so the test of this criterion runs on a11y-on and the a11y-off run records what it measures. (10) known-violations.json lists 12 findings on /: per build the three color-contrast lines and six target-size ones for the slideshow's dots (.w-5 and Slide 1 to Slide 5, 6 each build, so 12 in all). This slice is not meant to clear them: the manifest does not list the file; the slideshow stays with the switch off, so the a11y-off entries stay true; test/unit/browser-test-wiring.test.ts (line 437) fails unless a11y-on and a11y-off list the same findings, so pruning one build's would fail it; and the Hero carousel follow-up (line 1472) gives the pruning to WS03 or step 32. With the switch on, smoke.spec.ts reports the six a11y-on target-size entries as listed but not found ('fixed ... remove it once it no longer appears'), which is a report and an annotation, not a failure. Leave the file alone, quote that report, and note that the two arrows (24 by 24 pixels) and the dots no longer exist under newLook. Nothing is added to the file. (11) The brief and the manifest differ, and the manifest wins as recorded. The spec's image pipeline (lines 315 to 317) names hero.png as well as the slides, and its file lists (line 330) say 'remove HeroSlideshow' and (line 310) 'delete the auto-advance'; the Decisions at lines 1004 to 1006 settle that hero.png is left out (nothing imports it), the slideshow stays for the flag-off path with the new look showing one still, and WS03 replaces the hero and deletes HeroSlideshow. Record the three as deviations from the spec. The spec also says sharp-based generator or vite-imagetools (line 340): the manifest chooses the script; no image plugin is added. Two calls are the slice's own, and are judgement calls for K's eye: the still picture's alt text (the photo sits under the page's own heading as a darkened texture, as the slideshow's did, so the image is decoration with alt set to an empty string; DESIGN_REPLAN_phase0.md line 376 gives WS03's strip the words 'Players at long tables in a tournament hall' for the same photo, and slide 1 does show players at tables in a hall) and the label pill in the photo's top corner ('Louisiana Chess Community', HomePage.tsx line 82, drawn per slide today; keep slide 1's label in the still hero, so no words the page shows today vanish, and mark the call). (12) The picture cannot be found before the script runs, and the lab score may stay low. index.html has no preload and is not in this slice's files (adding a preload there would fire on every route and for the switch off); the page is a client-rendered app whose main chunk is 508,165 bytes (dist/assets/index-*.js) and which fetches the clearinghouse list and the clubs before drawing its lower bands, so the hero img exists only after the script runs, fetchpriority and all. The lab score is recorded as measured, with the lab check's own opportunities, and what it finds beyond the hero (the list fetches, the script size, the third-party feed band) goes to WS03 as a follow-up, as the manifest's risks say. K's own lab run on the preview is a follow-up for K. (13) The baseline and the step 32 note. test/a11y/baseline.ts samples / (and three other routes) on a11y-off with reduced motion and a 1280-pixel window: the page body, and inside main the first visible Button, th and .font-mono. On / the first Button is 'Find a tournament' in the hero (variant default, rgb(26, 39, 68) on rgb(200, 169, 74), Geist Variable), so with newLook off the hero's foreground, its Button and its order in the page must be as they are: the baseline's sha256 is ce04ac06f0b3906739738413ef7aa3a21b0e8b0b9e3fe1c09dbca15f9f4dcbef and must be the same afterwards.
